html:
Japan in the Sengoku, or Warring States, period, when the shoguns' power had collapsed and local lords fought for land. The map shows it in 1530 and 1600.

The Ōnin War of 1467 to 1477 ruined Kyoto and left the Ashikaga shoguns powerless. Across the country, warlords called daimyo built castles, raised peasant armies and made their own laws. In 1543 Portuguese traders brought firearms, which Japanese smiths soon copied, and in 1549 Francis Xavier brought Christianity.

Three men then unified the country. Oda Nobunaga seized Kyoto and broke the warrior monks, until he was killed in 1582. Toyotomi Hideyoshi finished the conquest in 1590, disarmed the peasants in the sword hunt and twice invaded Korea in the Imjin War. After his death Tokugawa Ieyasu won the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600 and became shogun in 1603, starting the long peace of Tokugawa Japan.
sum: Japan in the Sengoku, or Warring States, period, when the shoguns' power had collapsed and local lords fought for land. The map shows it in 1530 and 1600.
